chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Hisan, from Ibrahim ibn Asim ibn Hameed, from Salih ibn Maysam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three qualities: whoever possesses them has perfected the qualities of faith: whoever is patient with oppression, restrains his anger and counts it as a reward (from God), and pardons and forgives, will be among those whom God admits to Paradise without reckoning, and He will accept his intercession on behalf of as many people as there were in the tribes of Rabi'ah and Mudar.

key_terms.وَحْتَسَبَ: and counted it as a reward

ai.seo_question: What are the three qualities that perfect faith and guarantee entry to Paradise without reckoning?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three traits—patience under oppression, anger restraint with hope in reward, and forgiveness—as the pinnacle of Iman, linking them to the rare status of entering Paradise without the detailed reckoning (Hisab) mentioned in eschatological traditions. This specific combination emphasizes active moral agency in social conflicts, reflecting the Shia emphasis on character refinement (Takhalluq) as a means of spiritual elevation and communal influence.
